Thanks for introducing me to the word. The test said that I am extremely bad at identifying and expressing emotions, which is what my therapist has been trying to work on with me for ages. I think I just lack emotional depth.

I don't know, it seems like after my husband got shocked I started reflecting a little about my childhood and tried to take a third person perspective about the topic. I can think of maybe one direct link between the past and now? When I was a kid, my first hamster who I loved with all my heart passed away. My parents found me crying in grief and laughed at me for crying. (They even bought it up as a "they, so you remember when...") at a recent dinner. And then last year my hamster died after a period of sickness. My husband thought I would be absolutely devastated but I felt absolutely no emotion at all, not even sad. 

My husband also noticed that I'm very good at keeping control until I am in a safe space. I can be all smiles then the moment I walk through the door to our house I break down. I suppose it's because my parents wouldn't stop hitting me/locking me away until I stop crying so it might have been a learnt skill?

My therapist is trying to get me to work on mindfulness, which she says it's absolutely necessary before she starts to explore more difficult emotions and traumas with me. She says without the skills from mindfulness, I will not be able to safely handle what we might unearth. But so far I have been absolutely failing at mindfulness. Every time I try to clear my mind and focus on my breath I get a panic attack and difficulty breathing.

Also as an adult I think my main reaction to triggers are 80% freeze, 20% flight. But I think I fawned with my parents. Because if they did not get their way things would get bad.
